title: Who Said Neural Networks Aren't Linear?
claim: A linear operator sandwiched between two invertible networks defines new vector spaces under which the whole nonlinear map is linear.
layout: 3 panels: top-left pipeline, bottom-left spaces, right stacked operation diagrams
description: The figure has three dashed-border regions on a white background, all drawn in grey rounded boxes with black arrows. The top-left region shows f(x) as a left-to-right chain: input x goes into a dark grey box g_x, then through a matrix A (M×N), then into a box g_y^{-1}, and out as y. The whole chain sits inside a light grey rounded container. Below it, a second region shows two small maps: R^N goes through g_X back to R^N, and R^M goes through g_Y back to R^M. The right column has two stacked containers. The upper one is titled x1 ⊕_x x2. Inputs x1 and x2 each pass through g_x, are summed with +, and then go through g_y^{-1}. The lower one is titled a ⊙_x x. Input x passes through g_x, is multiplied by a scalar a, and goes through g_y^{-1}. The eye lands first on the large f(x) pipeline.
caption: Left. The Linearizer structure (top) is a linear operation sandwiched between two invertible functions (bottom). Right. Vector addition and scalar multiplication define induced vector spaces for which f is linear. (a) (b) (a) (b)
abstract: Neural networks are famously nonlinear. However, linearity is defined relative to a pair of vector spaces, $f:X \to Y$. Leveraging the algebraic concept of transport of structure, we propose a method to explicitly identify non-standard vector spaces where a neural network acts as a linear operator. When sandwiching a linear operator $A$ between two invertible neural networks, $f(x)=g_y^{-1}(A g_x(x))$, the corresponding vector spaces $X$ and $Y$ are induced by newly defined addition and scaling actions derived from $g_x$ and $g_y$. We term this kind of architecture a Linearizer. This framework makes the entire arsenal of linear algebra, including SVD, pseudo-inverse, orthogonal projection and more, applicable to nonlinear mappings. Furthermore, we show that the composition of two Linearizers that share a neural network is also a Linearizer. We leverage this property and demonstrate that training diffusion models using our architecture makes the hundreds of sampling steps collapse into a single step. We further utilize our framework to enforce idempotency (i.e. $f(f(x))=f(x)$) on networks leading to a globally projective generative model and to demonstrate modular style transfer.
